title: Postgres SQLi to COPY FROM PROGRAM Command Execution
learning_objectives: Recognise a database superuser account in a containerised stack as a critical mis-configuration
Use stacked queries through a simple-query-protocol sink (asyncpg .execute) that a prepared-statement sink (.fetch) would reject
Abuse Postgres COPY ... FROM PROGRAM (superuser only) to execute shell commands inside the database container
Read command output back through a temp table and a UNION on the visible query endpoint
Understand why the RCE stays risk:low: it needs no added Linux capabilities and is contained by cap_drop:ALL + read-only rootfs + a no-egress network
flag_hint: SQLi -> stacked CREATE TABLE + COPY loot FROM PROGRAM 'cat /labflag/flag.txt' (RCE inside the Postgres container) -> UNION-read the loot table -> POST /solve {"flag":"FLAG{...}"}. The flag is planted on the Postgres container filesystem (not in any table), so only command execution recovers it.
inspired_by: Adrien Peter's Postgres COPY FROM PROGRAM RCE research and subsequent HackerOne reports (e.g. GitLab #827052); abstracted, no vendor code reproduced
